## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
plot(1:10, type = 'o', main = "A Simple Plot")
```


```{r}
#| label: computing-environment
# Computing environment: where, and from which commit, this notebook ran
git <- function(args) {
  paste(system2("git", args, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE), collapse = "\n")
}
changed <- git(c("status", "--short", "--untracked-files=no"))

cat("Host:         ", Sys.info()[["nodename"]], "\n")
cat("Working dir:  ", getwd(), "\n")
cat("Git remote:   ", git(c("remote", "get-url", "origin")), "\n")
cat("Git commit:   ", git(c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")), "\n")
cat("Changed files:", if (nzchar(changed)) changed else "none", "\n")
sessionInfo()
```
